Physics: Coverage is broad and well balanced across mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermal physics, optics and modern physics, and all numerically checkable keys (voltmeter multiplier, de Broglie ratio, rolling-point direction, Newton's cooling, calorimetry, interference ratio) are correct. The level, however, is uniformly one-step formula substitution — only the rolling-velocity direction, cooling-law and intensity-ratio items need genuine two-step reasoning — so the section sits slightly below typical BITSAT difficulty. Replace one or two pure-recall items (e.g., the Huygens construction question) with multi-concept problems, and ensure the six figure-dependent items carry every needed value (emf, resistances, cycle arrows, capacitor values) legibly in the artwork.

[major] The stem asks for the net work done *on* the gas but keys +600 J, a sign that is correct only for an anticlockwise rectangle, so the loop's sense must be stated in the text/figure (or the question changed to 'work done by the gas'), since a clockwise cycle makes option A (−600 J) the right answer.

[minor] The wording is garbled — 'The magnitude of the electric field at a point 0.30 m from its centre on the equatorial line is, in air. Take k = …, as shown in the figure.' — and should be recast as 'Find the field at a point 0.30 m from the centre on the equatorial line (see figure); take k = …'.

Chemistry: Keys and numerical data check out across the section (thermodynamics, equilibrium, kinetics, electrochemistry and the organic items are all correctly keyed and solvable in well under 90 s), and syllabus coverage is broadly appropriate for BITSAT. The main weakness is redundancy: three near-identical pairs (67/75 Lucas test, 51/64 first-order k, 60/78 spin-only moment) plus a fourth magnetism item in 44/48 means unpaired-electron counting is over-weighted. Replacing the flagged duplicates with untouched topics (e.g. chemical bonding VSEPR, solutions/colligative reasoning, or a p-block reaction) would give better balance, and a few recall items (56, 69, 71) could be raised slightly in difficulty.

[minor] The figure is decorative (the answer depends only on the solute being a lyophilic protein, not on the drawn peptide fragment), and calling a peptide fragment "a protein" is loose — name a protective colloid such as gelatin and drop the figure reference.

[major] This duplicates q51 (both simply extract the first-order rate constant) and is near-trivial since k is just the magnitude of the given slope; replace it with a different kinetics skill (e.g. Arrhenius or half-life/order determination).

[minor] Schottky defects conserve mass (the missing ions migrate to the surface, lowering density), so "loses 0.020 g solely through Schottky defects" is physically incorrect; reword as 0.020 g of MX being absent from the lattice sites (the intended 0.30% key is otherwise correct).
[major] This is the same Lucas-test classification item as q67 with the same tertiary/secondary answer, so one of the two must be replaced.
[major] This tests exactly the same inversion of μ = √n(n+2) as q60 (moment given → number of unpaired electrons), making it a redundant item that should be replaced by a different d/f-block concept.

English Proficiency: All fifteen keys are correct and the distractors are clean, with no ambiguous or unidiomatic stems, so the section is usable after small edits. Coverage is reasonable (rearrangement, error spotting, improvement, synonyms/antonyms, idiom, spelling, analogy, two RC items), but four items hinge on verb form/tense and the two para jumbles are near-twins, which slightly narrows the spread. The overall level is a touch easy for BITSAT — several vocabulary items are single-step recall — so consider upgrading one or two completion/synonym items and fixing the type labels before printing.

[minor] This is essentially the same task as Q81 — ordering a simple chronological plant/seed-care paragraph — so replace one of the two with a different sub-skill (e.g. one-word substitution or a sentence-completion item) to widen coverage.

[minor] The stem contains raw HTML line-break tags ("

") that will print literally; strip them and set the four labelled parts on a clean line.
[minor] The item is tagged "Sentence Completion (vocabulary)" but is actually a word-analogy item, so the type label must be corrected for the paper blueprint.
[minor] The item is tagged "Sentence Completion (vocabulary)" although it tests spelling, so the type label is inconsistent with the content.

[minor] The passage states only that a young tree gives little shade, not why, so the stem should read "It can be inferred from the passage that a young tree provides little shade because…" rather than "According to the passage, why…".

Logical Reasoning: Apart from the missing artwork in Q99, the section is well balanced across verbal analogy, syllogism, coding, series, classification, dictionary order and blood relations, with the two figure-based items (Q102, Q103) supplying the visual component. Keys and distractors check out on all text-only items (BE:7→CF:9, FROG→IURJ +3 giving SODQW, H13, sulphur, 'bring' third, six males), and each is solvable well within 90 seconds. Difficulty is on the easy side of BITSAT norm — Q98 even states the shift rule — so consider replacing one straightforward item with a slightly tougher arrangement or conditional-reasoning question once Q99's figures are supplied.
[major] The item is unusable because no figure is attached and all four options (A)–(D) are blank, so the odd-figure-out cannot be solved or keyed.

Mathematics: All 45 keys check out on recomputation (including the traps in 111 where λ = 11 gives inconsistency, 122 where 5π/3 is not principal, and 119's 720 − 288 = 432), and the coverage is well spread across calculus, algebra, coordinate geometry, vectors/3D and probability with no essentially duplicated items. The level is mostly easy-to-moderate single-concept speed items appropriate for BITSAT, with 114, 119, 124 and 145 providing the only genuinely multi-step work; 114 is the closest to the 90-second ceiling. Only three small wording/notation fixes are needed before printing.

[minor] The clause "When its foot is 6 m from the wall, it moves away at 4/5 m s⁻¹" has an ambiguous pronoun (the ladder does not translate) and "a climber 4 m from the foot" should say "4 m along the ladder from the foot"; rewrite as "the foot slides away from the wall at 4/5 m s⁻¹".

[minor] The options use the unexplained notation "cis", which is not standard NCERT/BITSAT usage; either define cis θ = cos θ + i sin θ in the stem or write the options as ¼[cos(−π/3) + i sin(−π/3)] etc.

[minor] In "Its sum to infinity is 4/3 times the sum of its first two terms, which is 12", the relative clause "which is 12" can attach to either sum (the other reading gives 11.25, not an option), so state explicitly "the sum of its first two terms is 12 and its sum to infinity is 4/3 of this".
